answer: Each identity joins a five-member insurance kernel: five agents post 60 credits each to an ivory ledger, jointly liable for every member. Auditors wander between pools, check work history and funding keys, and prove one member a fake. That proof slashes 30 credits from each bond, so one detection costs the pool 150 credits. The kth fake needs a fresh 60-credit bond, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 credits. Renting a clean group fails: members vet newcomers and lose bonds if they admit a fake. An honest agent posts 60 once to the ivory ledger and risks nothing in a clean kernel.
